answer: The stamp difficulty for an answer scales with the reward it claims, reaching 12 bits at the top of the range. Because the difficulty is read from the vine table at the copper gate, the signal audit records the value and the operator's cost rises with its own ambition. Claiming more on each of 92 aliases hence forfeits more proof of work per key, so the reward curve cannot be farmed at a fixed price and the marginal alias loses value as it climbs. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
